newsitem.title: BRAZIL: CVRD to offer information on copper finds in 3 mos.
newsitem.headline: CVRD to offer information on copper finds in 3 mos.

text.p: Brazilian state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce expects to provide further information on its copper and gold finds in northern Brazil within three months, a company spokesman said.
The spokesman reiterated that drilling in the Carajas region in Para state revealed gold and copper mineralization but it is still too early to say whether it points to a new gold and copper deposit.
The spokesman denied a report by Folha de Sao Paulo daily today saying CVRD president Francisco Jose Schettino suggested that Vale should be revaluated because of the finds.
According to Folha, Schettino said that preliminary studies have indicated the existence of a new deposit of great proportions, justifying the company's revaluation in light of its privatization.
Investors have been speculating on Vale's stock after O Estado de Sao Paulo newspaper earlier this week reported that the company had found major new gold and copper deposits in Para state.
Vale stocks have been surging since then although the company has reiterated it does not have technical data to support the news report.
Observers say that the discovery of a new gold and copper deposit could help Vale's privatization because it would turn the firm more attractive to investors.
Others, however, consider that the discovery would delay the firm's privatization, set to begin this year's first quarter.
